clue.text: Work hard in attempt to get cup

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it, so the first pieces go inside the second

parts.note: an attempt is a try
OP is short for opus, a work
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An athlete is urged to put real effort in to win the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work hard' reads as one instruction, but it is two short pieces that go together inside the attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is very often a cup awarded to a winner, so the cup stands as an example.

clue.text: Wrong French river for this reptile

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the Oise is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: Someone has named the wrong French river when talking about a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: The tortoise is a slow land reptile with a domed shell, the creature the clue points to.

clue.text: Express an opinion in shop in Edinburgh

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their join

parts.note: read straight through the letters across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A customer voices a view inside a shop in the Scottish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is a formal verb for stating one's view, matching the phrase exactly.

clue.text: Thought twice, angry about rest

indicators.note: one word placed about another wraps around it on both sides

parts.note: heated means angry
to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: Someone paused before acting, cross about having to take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here means around, not concerning: the word for rest is wrapped by the word for angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hesitated paused in doubt, the same as having second thoughts before acting.

clue.text: I allow small number inside, in the dark

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something put inside another is enclosed by it

parts.note: to grant is to allow
No. is the short form of number

explanation.surface: Someone admits to letting a few things in without knowing anything about them.
explanation.walkthrough: No. is the printed abbreviation for number, which is why 'small number' gives two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark is an idiom for lacking knowledge, which is what ignorant means.

clue.text: Set of safety rules old codger screens once rewritten

indicators.note: text that is rewritten is set down again in a new order

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
taken as written, to be mixed with the letter before

explanation.surface: An elderly man vets a set of safety regulations after they have been redrafted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Green Cross Code is the British road-safety routine taught to children for crossing the street.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a short list of rules for crossing roads safely, so it is a set of safety rules.

clue.text: Some took a picture of rainforest animal

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lying inside them

parts.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the third

explanation.surface: A few visitors photographed a creature in the jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a striped giraffe relative living in the Congo rainforest.

clue.text: Plant high priest has first to ram into turf

parts.note: Aaron, brother of Moses, was the first high priest of Israel

indicators.note: something put into another ends up enclosed by it

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A biblical priest rams a plant into the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' joins the priest to the rest, and the possessive S of the answer comes from the turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's rod is a name for tall flowering plants such as great mullein, after the priest's staff that blossomed.

clue.text: Ambassador taken in by right-wing supposition

indicators.note: to be taken in by something is to be held within it

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right
HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A diplomat has been fooled by a conservative hypothesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests deceived, but it signals one piece held inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an idea put forward to explain something, a synonym for a supposition.

clue.text: Dish past age bracket, unfortunately

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written, all fourteen letters

explanation.surface: Someone sadly finds they are too old for a particular group.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpetbag steak is a thick steak stuffed with oysters, a meat dish.

clue.text: Restore control, say

parts.note: to rein is to control, as a horse
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone asks to have their authority given back, perhaps in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to put someone or something back in a former position, a synonym of restore.

clue.text: A nearly new suit

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
green means new or inexperienced, cut short by one letter

explanation.surface: A tailor's customer is offered a suit that is almost brand new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like a noun for clothing, but it is the verb, as in 'that suits me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that does not agree with you does not suit you, so the two verbs share a sense.

clue.text: Evident through time

parts.note: over can mean through or finished, as in 'the game is over'
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something becomes clear as time passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means openly shown rather than hidden, a synonym for evident.

clue.text: Italian boarding house, right for a senior citizen

parts.note: pensione is the Italian word for a guesthouse
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An Italian guesthouse is described as suitable for an elderly guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner is a retired person drawing a pension, the British everyday term for an older person.

clue.text: For example, cricket magazine's left

parts.note: The Spectator is a long-running British weekly magazine, here with its 's
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A magazine's cricket coverage is said to lean politically left.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket is a game people mostly enjoy by watching, an example of a sport for onlookers.

clue.text: Fourth letter in chart — see it any differently? The reason?

indicators.note: letters arranged differently are put in a new order
asks for just the letter at position four of the word that follows

parts.note: the fourth letter of the word
taken as written, to be mixed with the selected letter

explanation.surface: An optician asks a patient struggling to read the eye chart whether it looks any different.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the closing question: the reason a patient cannot read the chart might be tired eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, overworked eyes blur sight, so they could be why a letter on the chart is hard to read.

clue.text: Though no belle, she's always on the level!

definitions.text: Though no belle, she's always on the level!

parts.words: Though no belle, she's always on the level!
parts.note: surface reading: an unglamorous woman who is always honest; setter's reading: level also means flat or ordinary, the sense of an unadorned woman

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the level' reads as honest, but the setter means flat and unadorned, which is the first half of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a woman considered unattractive or ordinary in looks, which 'no belle' describes.

clue.text: New ruler etc. don provided

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A university teacher has been issued a new ruler and other stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like the verb to put on, but here it is a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a British university tutor or fellow, and such a person teaches as a lecturer.

clue.text: Name of deceased male found in a Tube train?

parts.note: a deceased male is a dead man, with 's from 'of'
handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: A corpse is discovered on the London Underground and someone asks who he was.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground; the definition is by example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead man's handle is a safety control that stops a train if the driver lets go, fitted in Underground cabs.

clue.text: Turn down quantity of steamed dumplings

parts.note: to dim is to turn down, as lights
a sum is a quantity or amount

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a portion of dumplings at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are small Cantonese parcels, typically steamed dumplings served in baskets.

clue.text: Preparation of ricin isn't essential

indicators.note: a preparation is something mixed or made up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A chemist notes that making the poison ricin is not necessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrinsic means belonging to the basic nature of a thing, a synonym for essential.

clue.text: Victor letting slip wife's secret

indicators.note: to let something slip is to lose hold of it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a victor is a winner
W is the abbreviation for wife, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A champion accidentally reveals his wife's private matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove W from WINNER. 'Letting slip' looks like revealing a secret, but it signals the dropped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private ones kept inside, so inner can mean secret.

clue.text: Piece of music individual found amongst books

indicators.note: something found amongst others is placed in their midst

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A single score is discovered among a pile of books.
explanation.walkthrough: Books in crosswords are usually the Old or New Testament, OT or NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a composition written for nine players, so it is a specific musical work.

clue.text: Trap quickly springs back — end of mouse!

indicators.note: something that springs back returns the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: soon means quickly, before long

indicators.note: end of asks for only the final letter of the next word

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A mousetrap snaps shut and that is the end of the mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope or wire that tightens, used as a snare to catch animals.

clue.text: Tell about a European country

indicators.note: one word about another surrounds it

parts.note: to spin a yarn is to tell a story
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to describe a country in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell about' looks like describe, but the verb is spin, as in spinning a story, wrapped around the a.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is the large country on the Iberian peninsula in south-west Europe.

clue.text: Last always, reportedly, to make an industrious effort

parts.note: the last part is the end

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by speech, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: ever means always, and its sound is spelt this way here

explanation.surface: Someone always comes in last, but by report they try very hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'end ever' matches the stressed sound of the answer, en-DEV-er.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to try hard to achieve something, a verb for making an earnest effort.

clue.text: Fellow explorer finds plant

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan explorer who sailed round the world

explanation.surface: A member of an expedition discovers a new plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrake is a Mediterranean herb with a forked root, famous in folklore.

clue.text: Nothing in measuring device can show falling star

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: a meter is a device for measuring
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An empty gauge is said to reveal a shooting star.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling of the measuring word is the one that works here, not metre.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a rock burning up in the atmosphere, popularly called a shooting or falling star.
